{{Short description|American (of Greek origin) physicist}}

'''Efstratios Manousakis''' (born July 11, 1957) is the Donald Robson Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[Florida State University College of Arts and Sciences|Florida State University]]. He is known for his contributions in the area of [[condensed matter physics]]. Among his works is his contribution to our understanding of the parent compound of the high-temperature [[cuprate superconductor]]s,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Manousakis |first=Efstratios |date=1991-01-01 |title=The spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on a square lattice and its application to the cuprous oxides |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.63.1 |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=63 |issue=1 |pages=1–62 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.63.1|bibcode=1991RvMP...63....1M |url-access=subscription }}</ref> which played a role in founding the relatively new field of quantum magnetism.

== Early life and education ==
Efstratios Manousakis was born on July 11, 1957, in [[Ithaca (island)|Ithaca]], Greece. He earned his undergraduate degree in 1980 from the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|University of Athens]] in Greece.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Efstratios Manousakis |url=http://samos.martech.fsu.edu/vita/default.htm |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=samos.martech.fsu.edu}}</ref> He completed his doctorate in 1985 at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] under the supervision of V. R. Pandharipande and [[David Pines]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Department of Physics - Florida State University |url=https://physics.fsu.edu/person/efstratios-manousakis |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=physics.fsu.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1985-1987 he was a postdoctoral associate at the [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology School of Engineering|Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]<ref name=":1" />.In 1987 he was hired at the [[Florida State University College of Arts and Sciences|Florida State University]], first, at the Supercomputer Computations Research Institute and from 1988 as a Faculty in Physics.<ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
Manousakis demonstrated that the ground-state of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on the square lattice, unlike previous suggestions by [[Philip W. Anderson|Phil Anderson]]  that it is a [[Resonating valence bond theory|resonating valence bond state]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anderson |first=P. W. |date=1987-03-06 |title=The Resonating Valence Bond State in La2CuO4 and Superconductivity |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.235.4793.1196 |journal=Science |volume=235 |issue=4793 |pages=1196–1198 |doi=10.1126/science.235.4793.1196|pmid=17818979 |bibcode=1987Sci...235.1196A |url-access=subscription }}</ref> is instead characterized by long-range antiferromagnetic order.<ref name=":0" /> This happens despite the large-amplitude quantum-spin fluctuations expected to be present due to fact that we are dealing with low-spin and low-dimensionality. He also demonstrated that the behavior of the spin-fluctuations in the parent compounds of the high-temperature cuprate-superconductors can be described by the spin-1/2 square-lattice quantum antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model.<ref name=":0" /> Manousakis' calculations have also illuminated the nature and propagation of the hole quasi-particle in quantum [[Antiferromagnetism|antiferromagnets]] as a spin-[[polaron]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Zhiping |last2=Manousakis |first2=Efstratios |date=1992-02-01 |title=Dynamical properties of a hole in a Heisenberg antiferromagnet |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.45.2425 |journal=Physical Review B |volume=45 |issue=5 |pages=2425–2437 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.45.2425|pmid=10001766 |bibcode=1992PhRvB..45.2425L |url-access=subscription }}</ref> or as a string<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Manousakis |first=Efstratios |date=2007-01-08 |title=String excitations of a hole in a quantum antiferromagnet and photoelectron spectroscopy |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.75.035106 |journal=Physical Review B |volume=75 |issue=3 |article-number=035106 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.75.035106|arxiv=cond-mat/0702288 |bibcode=2007PhRvB..75c5106M }}</ref> and these works have more recently found further application in the area of [[Ultracold atom|ultra-cold atoms]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Homeier |first1=Lukas |last2=Lange |first2=Hannah |last3=Demler |first3=Eugene |last4=Bohrdt |first4=Annabelle |last5=Grusdt |first5=Fabian |date=2025-01-02 |title=Feshbach hypothesis of high-Tc superconductivity in cuprates |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=16 |issue=1 |page=314 |doi=10.1038/s41467-024-55549-4  |doi-access=free|pmid=39747881 |issn=2041-1723|pmc=11696692 |arxiv=2312.02982 |bibcode=2025NatCo..16..314H }}</ref>

In 2010, he has proposed that efficient [[Solar cell|solar cells]] could be made using [[Strongly correlated material|strongly correlated materials]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Manousakis |first=Efstratios |date=2010-09-10 |title=Photovoltaic effect for narrow-gap Mott insulators |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.82.125109 |journal=Physical Review B |volume=82 |issue=12 |article-number=125109 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.82.125109|arxiv=0911.4933 |bibcode=2010PhRvB..82l5109M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Coulter |first1=John E. |last2=Manousakis |first2=Efstratios |last3=Gali |first3=Adam |date=2014-10-30 |title=Optoelectronic excitations and photovoltaic effect in strongly correlated materials |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.90.165142 |journal=Physical Review B |volume=90 |issue=16 |article-number=165142 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.90.165142|arxiv=1409.8261 |bibcode=2014PhRvB..90p5142C }}</ref> utilizing the concept of [[Multiple exciton generation|carrier multiplication]] via [[impact ionization]]. This idea has recently received theoretical and experimental attention.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gazzaneo |first1=Paolo |last2=Arrigoni |first2=Enrico |date=2025-03-01 |title=Phonon effects, impact ionization and power conversion in Mott photovoltaic systems |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=27 |issue=3 |page=033008 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/adb877 |arxiv=2408.14822 |bibcode=2025NJPh...27c3008G |issn=1367-2630|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sahu |first1=S. R. |last2=Khan |first2=S. |last3=Tripathy |first3=A. |last4=Dey |first4=K. |last5=Bano |first5=N. |last6=Raj Mohan |first6=S. |last7=Joshi |first7=M. P. |last8=Verma |first8=S. |last9=Rao |first9=B. T. |last10=Sathe |first10=V. G. |last11=Shukla |first11=D. K. |date=2023-09-21 |title=<nowiki>Multiple exciton generation in ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$</nowiki> |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.108.125133 |journal=Physical Review B |volume=108 |issue=12 |article-number=125133 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.108.125133|arxiv=2310.14835 }}</ref>

He has calculated<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Manousakis |first1=E. |last2=Pandharipande |first2=V. R. |date=1984-11-01 |title=Theoretical studies of elementary excitations in liquid He 4 |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.30.5062 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=30 |issue=9 |pages=5062–5075 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.30.5062 |issn=0163-1829|url-access=subscription }}</ref> the quasi-particle phonon-[[roton]] spectrum in [[Superfluid helium-4|superfluid <sup>4</sup>He]] that introduce corrections to previous calculations by [[Richard Feynman|Feynman]] and Cohen.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Feynman |first1=R. P. |last2=Cohen |first2=Michael |date=1956-06-01 |title=Energy Spectrum of the Excitations in Liquid Helium |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRev.102.1189 |journal=Physical Review |volume=102 |issue=5 |pages=1189–1204 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.102.1189|bibcode=1956PhRv..102.1189F |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This is discussed by [[David Pines]] in the book entitled ''Most of the Good Stuff: Memories of Richard Feynman''.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Most of the good stuff: memories of Richard Feynman |date=1993 |publisher=American Institute of Physics |isbn=978-0-88318-870-5 |editor-last=Feynman |editor-first=Richard P. |location=New York |editor-last2=Brown |editor-first2=Laurie M. |editor-last3=Rigden |editor-first3=John S.}}</ref>

Manousakis  has also worked on the nature of [[consciousness]] and its possible relation to quantum theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Manousakis |first=Efstratios |date=2006-09-27 |title=Founding Quantum Theory on the Basis of Consciousness |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10701-006-9049-9 |journal=Foundations of Physics |language=en |volume=36 |issue=6 |pages=795–838 |doi=10.1007/s10701-006-9049-9 |issn=0015-9018|arxiv=quant-ph/0604100 |bibcode=2006FoPh...36..795M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Manousakis |first=Efstratios |date=2009-11-01 |title=Quantum formalism to describe binocular rivalry |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0303264709000914 |journal=Biosystems |volume=98 |issue=2 |pages=57–66 |doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2009.05.012 |pmid=19520143 |issn=0303-2647|arxiv=0709.4516 |bibcode=2009BiSys..98...57M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web  |date=17 October 2007 |title=Could quantum effects explain consciousness? |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg19626264-000-could-quantum-effects-explain-consciousness/  |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=[[New Scientist]]|url-access=subscription |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-11-02 |title=A quantum theory of dreams? |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/science/science-news/3312624/A-quantum-theory-of-dreams.html |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=The Telegraph |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2017 he was elected [[fellow]] of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 AAAS Fellows Recognized for Advancing Science {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/news/2017-aaas-fellows-recognized-advancing-science |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref> in 2002 named fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2025-07-15 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> and in 2008 named Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name=":1" />
